system:
You read part of an interview. An analyst asked one future user of a software service a series of questions. You decide, for each question, whether it follows up the answer given just before it.

A question follows up the previous answer when it asks about something that answer said: it asks the speaker to explain, give an example of, say more about, or say why of something the answer mentioned, or it picks up a particular thing the answer named. Wording does not matter; a question can follow up an answer without repeating any of its words.

A question does not follow up the previous answer when it turns to something that answer did not mention, even if the speaker said it in an earlier answer, even if it stays with the same broad subject, and even if it is a good question. A general question that could follow any answer, such as whether there is anything else, does not follow up either.

You receive the pairs of the interview after its first question: for each later question, the answer given just before it, and the question.

Reply with JSON only: an object with one key, "questions", a list with exactly one entry for every pair, in the same order. Each entry has "id", the question's id, and "follow_up", true or false.

Q2
The answer just before it: The desk enters every closure the authorities announce. Planned ones come with a start and an end, sudden ones apply at once.
The question: What is different for you about a sudden closure?

Q3
The answer just before it: There is no time. It has to be in before the first drone reaches the area, and the companies need to see it straight away.
The question: How often do closures change during the day?

Q4
The answer just before it: Often. An area gets wider, or the end time moves.
The question: When the end time moves, what do you have to do?

Q5
The answer just before it: Enter the new version. The old one should stop counting from then on.
The question: What do you want to know after you have entered a closure?

Q6
The answer just before it: How much trouble it caused across the customers. Not whose drones, just how many flights it hit.
The question: Why not whose drones?

Q7
The answer just before it: That is their business. We have no reason to look into one company's operations.
The question: Who do you hand work to?

Q8
The answer just before it: Nobody really. The companies act on what we enter.
The question: What was the worst day for the desk recently?

Q9
The answer just before it: A closure was entered with the wrong end time and three companies kept their drones on the ground all afternoon.
The question: How was the wrong end time noticed?

Q10
The answer just before it: One of the companies phoned us to ask why it was still on.
The question: What does the desk check by hand today?

Q11
The answer just before it: That the area we entered is the one the authorities meant. We read it back against their notice.
The question: Can you give me an example of an area that did not match the notice?
